title: Salesforce Pricing 2026: The API Isn't in the $100 Plan
text:
10.11.2026 by Omar Abdalla 

Salesforce prints $25 and $100 per user on its small business page, and a team of five can end up well past either number. The bill changes the day your team wants a forecast, a few automations or a link to the tools your leads come from.

Salesforce costs $0 for 2 users on Free Suite, $25 per user a month on Starter Suite, $100 on Pro Suite and $195 to $550 on Core, Advanced and Max, billed annually above Starter. A team needing API access pays $125 per user on Pro Suite. Fluid CRM is one plan at $16 per seat per month.

## Salesforce Pricing Plans, With API Access and Flow Limits

Salesforce sells six plans. The first three are its small business suites, and Core, Advanced and Max are the Sales Cloud editions built for bigger sales teams.

| Plan | Price per user per month | Billing | API access | Flow automation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free Suite | $0 | Free, 2 user licenses | No | No |
| Starter Suite | $25 | Monthly or annually | No | Built-in sales flows only |
| Pro Suite | $100 | Annually, contract required | Extra $25 per user per month | 5 flows per org |
| Core | $195 | Annually | Included | Included |
| Advanced | $395 | Annually | Included | Included |
| Max | $550 | Annually, through sales | Included | Included |

Free Suite comes with two user licenses and stays free as long as someone logs in at least once every 60 days. It also caps email at 100 sends a month, and a third seller needs a paid plan.

Starter Suite has no user maximum on Salesforce’s own pricing page, so a team can add an eleventh seller without changing plan.

...

The API is how other software reads and writes your Salesforce data. Salesforce calls it the Web Services API, and its own comparison table lists it as not included on Free Suite or Starter Suite, an extra $25 per user per month on Pro Suite and included from Core.

...

Starter Suite comes with built-in sales flows and lead routing but no Flow Builder, Pro Suite allows 5 flows per org and Core removes the limit.

...

| Setup | Per user per month | 3 sellers, year one | 5 sellers, year one | 10 sellers, year one |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Starter Suite | $25 | $900 | $1,500 | $3,000 |
| Pro Suite | $100 | $3,600 | $6,000 | $12,000 |
| Pro Suite with the API add-on | $125 | $4,500 | $7,500 | $15,000 |
| Core | $195 | $7,020 | $11,700 | $23,400 |
| Core with Agentforce for Sales | From $320 | From $11,520 | From $19,200 | From $38,400 |

The jump that catches small teams is the second step. Starter to Pro with the API is five times the seat price, and it comes with an annual contract instead of a monthly bill.

That contract point is worth planning around. Starter Suite is the only paid Salesforce plan you can pay month to month, so a team that wants to test Salesforce for a quarter can only do it on Starter.

Salesforce labels the Starter and Pro prices as starting prices, with transaction fees applying. The rows above are the seat cost and nothing else.

...

How much does Salesforce cost per user per month?

Salesforce Starter Suite costs $25 per user per month, Pro Suite $100, Core $195, Advanced $395 and Max $550. Every plan above Starter is billed annually. Pro Suite with the Web Services API add-on comes to $125 per user per month.

...

No. Salesforce’s comparison table lists the Web Services API as not included on Starter Suite. It is an extra $25 per user per month on Pro Suite and included from Core.

...

- Starter Suite if leads come in through Salesforce’s own forms and by hand, and you don’t need a forecast. Budget $300 per seller a year.
- Pro Suite with the API if you need a forecast or quotes and a cold email tool or automation platform has to write into Salesforce. Budget $1,500 per seller a year, on a contract.
- Core if you need more than five flows, approval processes or Agentforce. Budget $2,340 per seller a year before any AI.

title: Salesforce Essentials: Migration and Starter Suite · Ask Quokka
text:
On this page

Salesforce Essentials has reached end of renewal. Salesforce's published migration path takes existing Essentials customers to Pro Suite. For a small US business evaluating a new CRM, Starter Suite is a separate current product choice, starting at $25 per user per month. Don't treat those two decisions as the same upgrade.

...

The official Essentials migration timeline establishes the transition to Pro Suite. Salesforce announced retirement on February 11, 2026. End-of-Renewal was August 18, 2026, and technical support ended September 18, 2026.

Salesforce also states that customers needed to consent to the Pro Suite upgrade by their contract end or August 18, whichever came first. Its notice says customers who didn't consent would lose access to their organization and data. An existing customer should check their account's migration status and contract rather than assume the old subscription continues unchanged.

These dates matter more than an old Essentials review or rate. A new buyer should evaluate the current product. An existing customer needs the migration terms applying to their organization.

...

Starter Suite combines sales, service, marketing, and commerce functions for a small business. Pro Suite adds deeper customization and more advanced workflow options. The named feature and edition should be checked together.

...

## Current subscription costs for a small team

Prices checked on October 16, 2026. The current Salesforce sales pricing page lists Starter Suite from $25 USD per user per month, billed monthly or annually. Pro Suite starts at $100 per user per month, billed annually, with an annual contract required.

| Current product | Starting subscription basis | Relevant buying question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starter Suite | $25 per user per month, monthly or annual billing | Do the packaged sales, service, marketing, and commerce workflows fit? |
| Pro Suite | $100 per user per month, billed annually | Does the team need the deeper customization, forecasting, and workflow scope? |

These are current public starting rates, not a statement of an existing Essentials customer's migration contract. Check that customer's order and upgrade terms separately. Add usage, optional products, applicable support, and implementation work when relevant.

For an itemized wider comparison, see Salesforce pricing. A subscription rate is only one part of deciding whether the workflow suits the team.

...

### How much is Salesforce Starter Suite?

Starter Suite starts at $25 USD per user per month, with monthly or annual billing. The price is a current public starting rate and can change with additional usage or products. It isn't the migration price for an existing Essentials contract.

title: Best Salesforce SMS App for Outbound Sales Teams
text:
TL;DR: The best Salesforce SMS app is decided by two things the roundups skip: which Salesforce object the app writes a text to, and what unit it bills you in. Salesforce’s own messaging for Sales needs Digital Engagement and logs conversations as sessions rather than Tasks, which means an activity report built on Tasks cannot see your reps’ texting at all. Pricing is worse, because no two vendors sell the same unit. Read first-hand on November 9, 2026: 360 SMS App lists $7 per user per month on annual billing with carrier fees billed separately per segment and states it is 100% native with no data leaving your org. ValueText lists $7 per user per month for Essential, but Essential is one-way and does not include receiving replies, and every plan carries a $499 per account per year base fee on top. Mogli charges nothing per user at all, listing $5,200 a year for 50,000 annual message segments and three numbers, $10,150 for 150,000 segments, and unlimited users per org on annual contracts. Salesmsg lists $25 a month for Basic and $277 for Pro with the first seat and number free, then $10 per extra seat, and prices in credits where one SMS credit is 160 characters. That 160 is the real unit everywhere, and it is fragile: per Twilio, a GSM-7 message fits 160 characters alone or 153 per part once it splits, and a single emoji or curly quote switches the message to UCS-2 and drops the limit to 70 characters, or 67 per part. Before any app, Salesforce Service Cloud itself lists $25 per user per month for Starter Suite, $100 Pro Suite, $195 Core, $395 Advanced and $550 Max, with additional messaging channels sold separately and no price published for them on that page. So ignore the “starting at” column, pick your object, count your segments, and make every vendor quote the same workload.

...

## What Salesforce charges before any SMS app is installed

It helps to size the app spend against the platform it sits on. As of November 9, 2026, Salesforce’s Service Cloud pricing page lists Starter Suite at $25 per user per month, Pro Suite at $100, Core at $195, Advanced at $395 and Max at $550, with everything except Starter Suite billed annually.

Messaging is not simply included at the top. The page lists Digital Channels as available for purchase on certain editions, and describes Max as including Web Chat with additional channels available for purchase. It does not publish a price for those additional channels.

So the honest comparison is not “app versus free native texting.” It is an app at $7 to $21 per user per month against a channel add-on, on top of an edition that already costs $195 or more per user per month at those November 2026 list prices, that writes to a different object and carries no published list price. That is worth a quote from your account executive before you assume the native path is the cheap one.

title: Salesforce Pricing UK 2026: List Prices and Renewal | PEF
text:
Salesforce’s UK list prices as published on salesforce.com in November 2026, product by product, what the per user figure leaves out, and the points I would press at renewal. Written by an independent adviser who sells no licences.

...

## Sales Cloud and Service Cloud UK list prices, November 2026

I checked the UK pricing pages on salesforce.com on 9 November 2026. Salesforce quotes every figure per user per month and, for everything above Starter Suite, requires an annual contract paid in advance. The pages say nothing about VAT, so I treat every figure as before VAT.

- Starter Suite: £20 per user per month, billed monthly or annually, transaction fees apply.
- Pro Suite: £80 per user per month, billed annually, contract required.
- Core: £156 per user per month, billed annually. This is the edition Salesforce says replaces Enterprise.
- Advanced: £316 per user per month, billed annually, replacing Unlimited.
- Max: £440 per user per month, billed annually, replacing the Agentforce 1 edition.

Service Cloud is priced at exactly the same five points, with case management and a self service help centre in Core, an AI agent for service in Advanced, and the contact centre and IT service features reserved for Max. Core, Advanced and Max were announced on 6 September 2026 at 195, 395 and 550 US dollars in the United States; the UK figures are Salesforce’s own sterling list. Salesforce’s statement that existing customer pricing on legacy editions remains unchanged matters: nobody on Enterprise or Unlimited is being forced onto the new tiers at renewal.

The new editions bundle things that used to be sold separately. Premier Success is included from Core upwards, where Pro Suite customers pay for it as an add on. Core and Advanced include Slack Business+ and Max includes Slack Enterprise+. Each edition carries an annual pool of Flex Credits for Agentforce: 500,000 on Core, one million on Advanced and 2.75 million on Max, per org per year. Every edition from Core up includes one partial copy sandbox; Advanced and Max add one full sandbox, which Core customers buy separately.

...

Salesforce’s Main Services Agreement, last updated on 15 September 2025, sets the frame. Subscriptions renew automatically for further one year terms unless either party gives written notice at least 30 days before the end of the term. Quantities cannot be decreased during a term. Anything sold at a promotional or one time price renews at Salesforce’s list price in force at the time, and if you reduce volume or term length at renewal Salesforce may reprice what remains. There is no cap on renewal increases in the MSA itself, so any price protection you want lives in your order form or nowhere.

...

1. Diary the notice date and start the work four months before it.
2. Count licences actually used, not assigned. Company Information and Login History in Setup will tell you, and a Salesforce health check turns that into evidence.
3. Ask for a written renewal cap and for the removal of any clause that resets promotional pricing to list.
4. Treat the move from Enterprise or Unlimited to Core or Advanced as a new purchase. Salesforce has said legacy pricing is unchanged, so compare what you pay today with the new tier before accepting a bundle you did not ask for. Agentforce 1 customers can move to Max at no extra cost.
5. Price Agentforce on Flex Credits or on the per user add on, whichever your usage model favours, and insist on a usage report before the second year.
6. Align end dates so that Sales, Service, Marketing and any portal renew together; separate dates remove your bargaining power one product at a time.

...

How much does Salesforce cost per user in the UK?

On salesforce.com’s UK pages in November 2026, Sales Cloud and Service Cloud list at £20 per user per month for Starter Suite, £80 for Pro Suite, £156 for Core, £316 for Advanced and £440 for Max, billed annually for everything above Starter. Those are list prices before VAT and before add ons such as Agentforce for Sales from £100 per user per month. Negotiated prices are set in your order form and are not published.

What is the difference between Salesforce Core, Advanced and Max?

They are the three editions Salesforce launched on 6 September 2026 to replace Enterprise, Unlimited and Agentforce 1. Core is the base edition with Premier Success, Slack Business+ and 500,000 Flex Credits a year. Advanced adds a full sandbox, the security and backup bundle and one million credits. Max includes Agentforce for Sales or Service, Agentforce Coworker, Slack Enterprise+ and 2.75 million credits. UK list prices are £156, £316 and £440 per user per month.
query: Salesforce Starter Suite pricing change or new launch announcement

# Salesforce Launches SMB Growth Kit: Everything You Need to Know

6 min read

Salesforce just made a move that's worth paying attention to if you run a small or growing business. On July 16, 2026, the company announced its SMB Growth Kit, a bundled offering built specifically for small and medium businesses in India, combining Agentforce Sales, Slack, and Tableau into a single connected platform. It's a fairly direct answer to a problem a lot of growing businesses know all too well, sales data in one place, team conversations in another, reporting scattered across spreadsheets nobody fully trusts.

...

The Growth Kit isn't a new product built from scratch, it's a curated bundle of three tools Salesforce already had, packaged specifically for SMB needs and priced and positioned to get a smaller business up and running fast. Agentforce Sales brings structure to the revenue side of the business, replacing the spreadsheets, manual updates, and "one person who knows where everything is" approach a lot of SMBs still run on, with a real-time view of every lead, opportunity, and pipeline stage. Slack handles the collaboration layer, keeping deal conversations and team coordination inside the same ecosystem as the sales data itself, rather than split across email threads and a separate chat app. Tableau rounds it out with drag-and-drop analytics, giving business owners visibility into performance without needing a dedicated data team or a separate BI tool bolted on afterward.

Salesforce is positioning the whole package around speed, the company says a business can go live in four to six weeks, delivered through select reseller partners with structured onboarding, hands-on setup, and post-go-live support built in, rather than leaving a small business to figure out implementation entirely on its own.

...

## What This Means for Salesforce SMB Pricing

Salesforce hasn't published a standalone price tag for the Growth Kit bundle specifically, but it's worth understanding where SMB pricing typically sits on Salesforce's broader platform, since that context matters for anyone evaluating the fit.

The entry point for Salesforce SMB CRM is the Starter Suite, priced at $25 per user per month on annual billing, covering core sales, service, marketing, and commerce tools, plus Slack included at no extra cost. For a small team of five users, that works out to roughly $1,500 a year in base license fees. If a business outgrows Starter Suite, the next step up is Pro Suite at $100 per user per month, a jump significant enough that plenty of SMBs find themselves stuck weighing whether they're ready for that increase before they're fully sure of it.

AI-forward plans that lean more heavily on Agentforce capabilities sit considerably higher, up to $550 per user per month for Agentforce 1 Sales editions, which is a meaningful gap from the entry-level tier. And license fees are genuinely only part of the real Salesforce for small business pricing picture, implementation costs for smaller businesses commonly run somewhere between $10,000 and $20,000 as a one-time fee, before ongoing licensing is even factored in. This is exactly the kind of total cost of ownership conversation the Growth Kit's guided onboarding is presumably meant to simplify, though the actual bundled pricing details will matter a great deal once they're made public.

title: Salesforce for Small Business: Cost, Plans and Setup
text:
- Sales Cloud - the core CRM product. Contact management, lead tracking, opportunity pipeline, email integration, basic reporting. This is the starting point for almost every small business that needs Salesforce
- Service Cloud - customer support management. Case tracking, support queues, customer self-service. Worth considering if you handle a significant volume of customer queries or after-sales support
- Starter Suite - Salesforce's bundled entry-level product at $25/user/month, which combines basic sales, service, marketing, and commerce tools under one SKU. Designed specifically for small teams who need a bit of everything without committing to individual clouds

...

## Salesforce CRM for Startups: What to Start With

For a startup or early-stage business, the Starter Suite is usually the right entry point. At $25/user/month, it gives you a working CRM with lead and contact management, basic pipeline tracking, email integration with Gmail or Outlook, mobile access, and a reporting layer, without the complexity of configuring individual clouds from scratch.

The Starter Suite is capped at 10 users, which works for most early-stage teams. When you outgrow it, either in team size or in the automation and customisation you need, the Pro Suite at $100/user/month is the natural next step. It removes the user cap and opens up significantly more workflow automation through Flow Builder.

...

text:
# Sell Your Full Portfolio on AgentExchange, in One Private Offer

 Ryan Dudak 

 Bharath Balasubramanian 

 November 10, 2026 3 min read 

Your business is bigger than the app you build on Salesforce. Your customers aren’t just buying software. They need the external platforms, implementation services, and support that turn software into business results. Until now, none of that could be sold alongside your managed package through AgentExchange. Now it can: for the first time, you can sell your app, external products, and professional services together in a single private offer on AgentExchange.

At Dreamforce, we shared the next evolution of AgentExchange, bringing apps, agents, skills, and MCP servers together in a unified marketplace to help customers discover and adopt partner innovation. AgentExchange Commerce helps turn that demand into revenue through private offers with tailored terms, simplified procurement, and consolidated billing.

This release is a major expansion of what partners can sell on AgentExchange. Three new capabilities make it easier to sell your full portfolio, structure longer-term deals, and simplify renewals.

Enlarge

## Sell your full portfolio, not just your managed package

With this release, you can bring eligible external products and services together with your managed package in a single private offer on AgentExchange. You can:

- Sell your full portfolio: Bundle managed packages, partner-hosted SaaS products, and professional services in one private offer.
- Monetize your expertise: Include consulting, implementation, training, and ongoing support alongside your software.
- Offer flexible pricing: Combine one-time charges for services with recurring software or support subscriptions in a single order.

Imagine a customer buying your Salesforce app, the external SaaS platform it connects to, implementation services, and a premium support plan, all through a single private offer. What once required separate purchases and invoices can now be sold together: one offer, one transaction, one invoice for everything your customer needs. With AgentExchange Commerce, consolidated billing and payment processing simplify the transaction. Licenses for your managed package are provisioned automatically and stay in sync with the order, while you continue delivering your external products and services.

...

## Two more ways to grow

- Close deals on your customers’ terms. Eligible partners can offer 24- or 36-month agreements with annual invoicing through private offers. Multi-year terms require account-level enablement, so contact your Salesforce Partner Account Manager to get started.
- Simplify every renewal. Start with a pre-populated offer from an existing order, with automated billing and supported license reconciliation at the contract anniversary. Partners and customers receive advance renewal notifications, with cadences configurable through Flow Builder.
